vocabulary.meaning_en: able to do something well because of training or practice
dealing with real situations in a sensible way
vocabulary.example: She gave me some practical advice.
He is determined to pass the exam.

vocabulary.meaning_en: not willing to change your mind
vocabulary.example: My little brother is very stubborn.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the joint in the middle of your leg
vocabulary.example: I hurt my knee playing football.

vocabulary.meaning_en: all the bones of a body
vocabulary.example: There is a dinosaur skeleton in the museum.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a group of people who work together, e.g. on a ship or plane
vocabulary.example: The crew welcomed us on the plane.
You need a minimum of five players.
A celebrity chef opened the restaurant.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the organ in your head that you think with
vocabulary.example: Reading is good for your brain.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the soft hair of sheep, used to make clothes
vocabulary.example: This jumper is made of wool.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to make someone believe something that is not true
vocabulary.example: He tricked me into paying for his lunch.

vocabulary.meaning_en: not wanting to work or make an effort
vocabulary.example: Don't be lazy – help me clean up.
The machines were idle during the holiday.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the hard part at the end of your finger; also a thin metal pin
to ask a price for something
vocabulary.example: They charged me £50 for the repair.

fine_lines.title: an old hand vs bone idle
fine_lines.explanation_ar: an old hand = شخص ماهر ومتمرّس في عمل ما (مديح). bone idle = كسول جداً (ذمّ). لاحظ: an old hand at + اسم/فعل بـ ing.
fine_lines.explanation_en: 'An old hand' is a skilled, experienced person (praise). 'Bone idle' means extremely lazy (criticism). Note: an old hand at + noun / -ing.

examples.sentence: Ask Mona – she's an old hand at fixing bikes.
He's bone idle; he never helps at home.

fine_lines.title: hard-nosed: two sides
fine_lines.explanation_ar: hard-nosed قد تكون مديحاً: عملي ومصمّم وصلب. وقد تكون ذماً: عنيد وقاسٍ لا يراعي المشاعر. السياق يحدد المعنى.
fine_lines.explanation_en: 'Hard-nosed' can be positive: practical, determined and tough. It can also be negative: stubborn and insensitive. The context tells you which.

examples.sentence: A hard-nosed reporter found the true story.
The hard-nosed manager refused to listen to anyone.

fine_lines.title: pull the wool over someone's eyes vs bleed someone dry
words: pull the wool over someone's eyes
fine_lines.explanation_ar: pull the wool over someone's eyes = يخدع شخصاً ويخفي الحقيقة عنه. bleed someone dry = يأخذ كل مال شخص تدريجياً (بأسعار عالية أو تكاليف مستمرة).
fine_lines.explanation_en: 'Pull the wool over someone's eyes' = trick someone and hide the truth. 'Bleed someone dry' = take all of someone's money, usually by charging too much.

examples.word: pull the wool over someone's eyes
examples.sentence: You can't pull the wool over my eyes – I know you didn't do your homework.
The repairs on this old house are bleeding us dry.

expressions.meaning_en: a very skilled and experienced person
expressions.example: My grandmother is an old hand at baking bread.

expressions.meaning_ar: عملي وصلب ومصمّم؛ أو عنيد وقاسٍ
expressions.meaning_en: practical, determined and tough; sometimes stubborn and insensitive
expressions.example: She's a hard-nosed businesswoman who always gets a good price.

expressions.meaning_en: a lively party, often with dancing
expressions.example: We had a big knees-up for Grandad's 80th birthday.

expressions.meaning_ar: أقل عدد من الموظفين يكفي لتشغيل العمل
expressions.meaning_en: the smallest number of workers needed to keep a business running
expressions.example: Over the holiday, the hospital office runs with a skeleton crew.

expressions.meaning_ar: عبارة مازحة بعد عمل جيد: «انظر يا فلان المشهور، أنا بمستواك!»
expressions.meaning_en: a joke after doing something well, comparing yourself to someone famous
expressions.example: Look at my cake! Eat your heart out, famous bakers!

expressions.meaning_ar: لحظة نسيان أو عدم قدرة على التفكير بوضوح
expressions.meaning_en: a short moment when you can't think clearly or remember something
expressions.example: I forgot my own phone number – total brain fade!

expressions.phrase: pull the wool over someone's eyes
expressions.meaning_en: to trick someone or hide the truth from them
expressions.example: The seller tried to pull the wool over my eyes about the car's age.
My cat is bone idle – she sleeps all day.

expressions.meaning_ar: يقاتل بكل قوته وإصراره للحصول على شيء
expressions.meaning_en: to use all your effort and determination to get or keep something
expressions.example: The villagers fought tooth and nail to save their library.

expressions.meaning_en: to take all of someone's money, often by charging too much
expressions.example: That old car is bleeding me dry with repairs.

grammar.title: Compound adjectives with hyphens: hard-nosed, bone idle
grammar.explanation_ar: الصفة المركّبة من كلمتين تُكتب غالباً بشرطة قبل الاسم: a hard-nosed reporter. نمط شائع: صفة + اسم + ed: hard + nose + ed = hard-nosed، kind-hearted، blue-eyed. أما bone idle فكلمة bone هنا تقوّي المعنى بمعنى «جداً»، كما في bone dry.
grammar.explanation_en: Two-word adjectives often use a hyphen: a hard-nosed reporter. A common pattern is adjective + noun + -ed: hard-nosed, kind-hearted, blue-eyed. In 'bone idle', 'bone' just makes it stronger (= very), like 'bone dry'.

questions.question: 'He's an old hand at fixing computers.' He is...
During the holiday, only three people worked in the office. It had a ___.
questions.explanation_ar: skeleton crew = أقل عدد من الموظفين.
questions.explanation_en: A 'skeleton crew' is the minimum number of workers.

questions.question: I forgot my best friend's name for a second! What a ___!
questions.explanation_en: 'Brain fade' is a moment when you can't remember.

questions.question: 'You can't pull the wool over my eyes.' The speaker means...
questions.explanation_ar: pull the wool over someone's eyes = يخدع.

questions.question: He never does anything. He just lies on the sofa. He's ___.
Complete: 'They fought ___ to keep the park open.'
questions.explanation_en: The idiom is 'fight tooth and nail'.

questions.question: 'This old house is bleeding us dry.' What is the problem?
choices: It costs us too much money.
questions.explanation_en: It means taking all your money.

questions.question: After painting a nice picture, Sara laughs: '___, Picasso!'
questions.explanation_ar: eat your heart out + اسم مشهور: مزاح بعد عمل جيد.
questions.explanation_en: 'Eat your heart out' + famous name is a joke after doing well.

questions.question: Which sentence uses 'hard-nosed' in a positive way?
choices: He is hard-nosed and never listens.
A hard-nosed reporter found the truth.
He has a hard nose from the accident.
